title: Compact Role Binding Quick Actions & Command Palette for Member Assignment
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As RBAC moves to v2 with more granular role templates and frequent role churn, product and platform teams need faster ways to assign, update, and audit role bindings for users and SSO groups. The current role editor flow requires multiple modal steps for common changes (e.g., quick assign a role, toggle temporary access window, link SSO group). This ticket explores a compact, keyboard-first command-palette and inline quick-actions UI for member assignment and role binding edits in the Console.

Goals:
- Reduce common bind/edit flows to 1–2 keystrokes or clicks for power users.
- Preserve safety for destructive changes (role removal, privilege escalation) with contextual confirmations.
- Surface audit links and SSO mapping hints inline so admins can validate origin of membership.
- Support accessibility (keyboard nav, screen reader labels) and mobile/responsive considerations.

Scope: Design of the compact role-binding row, command palette triggers and flows, inline permission preview, microcopy for warnings, and handoff artifacts for engineering (interaction spec and ARIA guidance). Not in scope: backend permission model changes or audit log storage; those are separate infra tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K) exposes 'Assign role to <user|group>' and fuzzy-searches users and groups by email/display name/SSO group id.
Quick-actions inline on each member row include: Edit role (shortcut E), Temporarily grant (clock icon), Link SSO group (if unresolved), and Remove binding (with staged confirm).
Inline permission preview shows the top 3 effective permissions for the binding and a link 'View full permissions' that opens the role inspector.
All destructive actions require a clear two-step confirmation (secondary button + typed confirmation for org-level Admin role removals).
Accessibility: every quick-action is reachable via keyboard, has an aria-label, and voiceover reads contextual warning when removing or escalating roles.
Telemetry: UI emits events for palette-open, quick-assign-success/failure, quick-remove-initiated, and confirm-completed for product analytics and regression monitoring.
Design handoff includes annotated Figma frames, interaction flow stubs, and an ARIA checklist in the developer notes.
design_notes:
Approach: Combine a lightweight command palette pattern with a compact member-row affordance to satisfy both power users and occasional admins. Palette results should prioritize least-privilege suggestions (e.g., recommend Read-only variants if ambiguous). Use color-coded badges for SSO-mapped bindings and show a small shield icon for elevated roles. For temporary grants, use a minimal calendar + quick presets (1h, 8h, 24h, 7d). Avoid modal stacking; inline editors or popovers preferred. Provide 'preview audit trail' link that opens right-hand inspection panel, not a full navigation change.

UX trade-offs considered:
- Inline editing reduces context-switches but increases row complexity; mitigate with hover-only affordances and progressive disclosure.
- Command palette accelerates repeat tasks but requires discoverability; add ephemeral hint text in the members list header and a short onboarding tooltip.

AR/Accessibility: Use role="button" on all clickable non-button elements, manage focus when popovers open, and ensure color is not the sole indicator of risk. Include a high-contrast mode for warning states.
decisions: Use single command-palette entrypoint (Cmd/Ctrl+K) rather than multiple hotkeys to reduce discoverability burden.
Temporarily granted roles are modeled as binding metadata (expiration timestamp) surfaced in the UI but enforced by backend task (not part of this ticket).
Inline permission preview will show 3 highest-impact permissions and link to full role inspector — prevents over-cluttering the member row.
blockers: Need mapping of SSO group metadata from identity provider (IDP) to show 'SSO source' badge — infra ticket dependency.
Backend API for quick-assign must support optimistic updates and rollback on failure; API contract pending.
Audit log deep-linking API to view relevant entries in an inspection panel is unimplemented.
